content:
zoe: Quick triage: onboarding with FluxCart — customers report 429s within ~15s of login. They reproduce locally: multiple tabs + service worker all call sdk.init() and token mint at once. Paste from their demo logs.

zoe: ```
[2026-04-05T11:05:02Z] tab-1 init /v1/preflight 200
[2026-04-05T11:05:03Z] tab-2 init /v1/preflight 429 x 11
[2026-04-05T11:05:03Z] sw mint /v1/token 429 x 6
[2026-04-05T11:05:04Z] tab-3 init /v1/preflight 429 x 9
```

rahul: Which SDK + auth? Do they mint tokens per-tab or share a dev key?

zoe: Browser SDK v1.8.3, onboarding used a shared server key for speed. No init splay and service worker mints synchronously on startup.

carmen: Definitely a fanout on both preflight and token endpoints. Short-term advice for customer: 1) switch to ephemeral token per-tab, 2) only mint on first visible tab, 3) add randomized init delay. Minimal jitter snippet to send them:```js
// jittered init + single-tab mint guard
if (sessionStorage.getItem('flux_mint_inflight')) return;
const jitter = 150 + Math.floor(Math.random()*900); // 150-1050ms
setTimeout(async ()=>{ if (document.visibilityState !== 'visible') return; sessionStorage.setItem('flux_mint_inflight','1'); try{ const token = await fetch('/_mint').then(r=>r.json()); await sdk.init({token}); } finally{ sessionStorage.removeItem('flux_mint_inflight'); } }, jitter);
```

rahul: Good. Ops-side we can also flip a tenant flag to reduce 429s ASAP: enable preflight_coalesce, enable token_mint_coalesce, and apply a transient burst_window increase (+180) and a 2s leaky-bucket smoothing on both routes. That should reduce pressure while they implement client changes.

rl-bot: RateLimitAlert: tenant=\"fluxcart\" window=2026-04-05T11:04:55Z..2026-04-05T11:07:00Z peak_preflight=170 req/min peak_mint=95 req/min. Suggested action: preflight_coalesce + token_mint_coalesce + burst_window=+180.

carmen: I'll ask for permission to apply a 1-hour TTL change. Also propose we provide them a tiny server-side mint-proxy example that coalesces mints at their backend if they can't switch to ephemeral tokens quickly. Example proxy pattern we can share:```js
// simple in-process coalescer
let pending = null;
async function mintCoalesced(){ if (pending) return pending; pending = fetch('https://api.redwood.internal/mint',{method:'POST'})
  .then(r=>r.json()).finally(()=> pending=null);
 return pending; }
```

zoe: Customer agreed to a short maintenance window and to accept the ops patch. They'll roll ephemeral token support within the hour. I'll schedule the window and send the client snippets + proxy pattern.

rahul: Post-change checklist: monitor 429 rate for 2 hours, sample 10 mint traces, verify token TTL ~60s and per-tab variance. If 429s remain after client and tenant coalesce, escalate to runtime for KV-cache and batching tuning.

zoe: Updating the onboarding ticket and looping SE for the rollout. Thanks :raised_hands:
